text:
Calgary outshot Anaheim in attempts 70 to 56, won the even-strength chance battle 2.46 to 2.08 in expected goals, and still lost 4-2. By the model's count, CGY deserved to win 59 percent of the time, and the gap came down to what each team did with its moments.

Anaheim scored on its first power play, when Jackson LaCombe snapped one home at 10:02 of the first, and added a deflection from Frank Vatrano at 19:15 to go up 2-1. Dustin Wolf finished 1.55 goals worse than expected, while Ville Husso stopped 0.94 more than the shots against him should have allowed. Aydar Suniev tied it late in the second off a low-percentage wrist shot (5 percent), a goal Calgary had barely earned.

The third period belonged to Anaheim, which produced 2.0 expected goals to Calgary's 1.0 after a combined 1.51 over the first two. Ryan Poehling put the Ducks ahead with a shorthanded snap shot at 5:35, a goal that came on Calgary's own power play, and Nikita Nesterenko poked in the fourth at 17:03 off feeds from Alex Killorn and Mikael Granlund. Calgary went 0-for-3 with the man advantage while Anaheim scored once on two chances and added the shorthanded goal. Poehling, with a goal and an assist in under 12 minutes, was named first star.
